newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU warns member states on citizenship legislation.
newsitem.headline: EU warns member states on citizenship legislation.

text.p: The European Commission served notice on Wednesday that it would not hesitate to take legal action against member states not complying with European Union legislation granting the block's citizens special rights.
The Commission adopted a report on EU citizenship, which was introduced by the 1992 Maastricht treaty.
Among other things, it gives nationals of EU member states the right to free movement and residence across the EU.
It also gives them the right to vote and stand for election in the European Parliament and municipal elections where they are living.
"Citizens are entitled to be aware of the rights conferred on them by the EU and to have these rights honoured in practice by member states," said EU Internal Market Commissioner Mario Monti.
However, several member states had not yet turned rules on, for example, municipal elections into national law.
"There are problems which are being solved in the three new member states, Sweden, Finland and Austria," Monti said.
France and Belgium had also not yet implemented the directive. The Commission had already taken the first step in an infringement procedure against Paris and Brussels, he said.
"In June we shall see if we need to take further steps," Monti told a press conference.
In addition, not all EU countries have introduced arrangements for providing consular protection in third countries to EU nationals whose own country is not represented.

Some member states have also not turned the EU directive on the right of entry and residence into national law. "As a result of which seven infringement proceedings are still outstanding," the Commission said.
Such proceedings against individual member states would continue to play a crucial role, especially where there were persistent problems and where member states refused to cooperate.

"The Commission will therefore continue to monitor constantly the application of Community law and follow up on individual complaints from citizens," it said, adding infringement proceedings should be further accelerated.
